From Ternate, the 14th of June, Year 1751.— Register of Papers, as by order of the Esteemed and Honorable Gentlemen Jan Elias van Mijlendonk, Governor and Director together with the Council of these Moluccas, by the ship Rust en Werk [Rest and Work] from here via Macassar to Batavia were sent, consigned and described to His High Nobility, the High and Noble well-born greatly Honored Lord Jacob Mossel.— Governor General, together with the late Esteemed Gentlemen Councilors of the Netherlands Indies. BB: This Register.— No. 1: An original missive signed by the Governor and Council in Molucco, to the aforementioned Your High Nobility, of this date— No. 2: Copy of a report concerning the Cruise undertaken toward the Coast of Mindanao and the Karinganise Islands— No. 3.— A Copy of a resolution taken in the Council of Policy at Ternate of the date 27th of August of the year past.— No. 4: Two pieces of drafts on the Ternate Trade books 487 of the year 1749, and 17 7/50.— No. 5:—. Reports of the Confrontation made on the same. From Ternate, the 12th of June, Year 1751.— No. 6: A Case with described Trade papers of the same years 17 7/49 and 17 25/50.— No. 7:— Same, same described Salary Papers of the year 17 7/50.— No. 8: The Collections or positive orders drawn from the successive [orders] through Your High Nobility to Ternate and the remaining Eastern Government and separated letters since the year 1739 to 1749, inclusive.— No. 9: An Original Signed Report from the under-Merchant and Small Cashier Jan Hendrik Borwater, and the bookkeeper and First-sworn Clerk of Policy Bastiaan Ruijbroeck concerning the Seizure of Gold Cloth made.— No. 10: Bill of Lading and invoice of the cargo loaded in the bringer hereof.— No. 11: Arrival record of this vessel Ternate in the Castle Orange on the 12th of June, Year 1751 [was signed] I.s Thornton, secretary.

Communication of the receipt of Your High Nobility's honored missive and enclosures. From Ternate, the 14th of June, Year 1751: Batavia. To His High Nobility, the High and Noble greatly Honored Lord Jacob Mossel.— Governor General, together with the well Esteemed Gentlemen Councilors of the Netherlands Indies. By the Ship Rust en Werk [Rest and Work] via Macassar. High and Noble, greatly Honored, Valiant, wise, prudent, Discreet, and most generous Lord Gentlemen.— Upon the arrival at this Roadstead of the ships De Galathea and Rust en Werk on the 12th of April and in the month of May of this year, we found ourselves honored and gladdened with Your High Noble greatly Honored original and duplicate Missive of the 31st of December of the year past with the thereto pertaining enclosures, according to the dictate of the register attached thereto, all of which being contained therein, the highly esteemed orders and commands, we take the liberty to assure Your High Noble greatly [Honored]— like shall be observed— General rescription to the— for congratulation to the new high and Noble Lord Governor General. From Ternate, the 14th of June, 1751. Which in our hands, Esteemed greatly Honored, in all respect we assure, that by us with all Industry and attentiveness pursued, and so far as possible is, shall be complied with, and that which since the dispatch of our previous year's submission advice, in the entire circumference of these Moluccas— at the same time— is done and executed, in the coming month of July or August, which of the nearest ships according to our meager ability, we shall endeavor to apportion to Your High Noble greatly Honored, and to report, meanwhile we the bringer hereof as speedily as possible has been, having caused his cargo to be unloaded, in accordance with Your High Nobility's order, now send via Macassar, and by that opportunity we take the Honor to congratulate our new chief commander, the high and Noble greatly Honored Lord Jacob Mossel, with his

the coming month of July or August, which of the nearest ships according to our meager ability, we shall endeavor to apportion to Your High Noble greatly Honored, and to report, meanwhile we the bringer hereof as speedily as possible has been, having caused his cargo to be unloaded, in accordance with Your High Nobility's order, now send via Macassar, and by that opportunity we take the Honor to congratulate our new chief commander, the high and Noble greatly Honored Lord Jacob Mossel, with his Nobility's assumed weighty General administration, from the bottom of our hearts, and to wish that God Almighty may be pleased to bless his High Nobility's Illustrious person with all desirable blessings, in Soul and Body, likewise that all his High Nobility's counsels and undertakings, to the Glory of his dear person and the best of the society, may be happy and prosperous. Whereupon we cannot refrain from reporting to Your High Noble greatly Honored how the Commission decreed in the year past toward the Coast of Mindanao and the Paringanise Islands, the division of the poor outcome of the voyage made, the quantity of goods collected there. From Ternate, the 10th of June, Year 1737. to our utmost regret against the Expectation which Your High Noble greatly Honored and we had thereof, has turned out, namely toward Mindanao.— those sent thither having been commissioned the under-merchant Johannes Pauwen and the Skipper of the Yacht De Geertruijda, Stephanus de Jager, under date the 11th of the month of September of the week past, have here again arrived at the roadstead, we from their [report] to our Meeting of the 5th of September, thereupon submitted, and to the resolution of that date inserted report, seen that they during that voyage could obtain no greater merchandise for the Esteemed Company than 45 pounds of wax, for as many pounds of iron, and 18 [pieces] of Caret or tortoiseshell for

the Jager, under date the 11th of the month of September of the week past, have here again arrived at the roadstead, we from their [report] to our Meeting of the 5th of September, thereupon submitted, and to the resolution of that date inserted report, seen that they during that voyage could obtain no greater merchandise for the Esteemed Company than 45 pounds of wax, for as many pounds of iron, and 18 [pieces] of Caret or tortoiseshell for a piece of blue Flag cloth, likewise that the aforementioned Commissioners contrary to the orders given to them, visited only a part of this Coast, and did not direct their course toward the Islands Hullok and Pagumna, under allegation and assurance that on the whole Coast of Mindanao and the Islands lying thereabout, there is absolutely no advantageous trade to be conducted for the Company, indeed this Land cannot in the least be trusted, but one must always be on guard lest by the same one be treacherously surprised and plundered, wherefore we on that day deemed it good and resolved to send the aforementioned report for the much esteemed consideration of Your High Noble greatly Honored, as the same now goes, and we take [note] of the aforementioned voyage whether it shall be resumed again.— the lease made of the Company's domains in this poor outcome.
